title: The Ledger
logline: A village shop's handwritten credit book holds decades of small debts, some paid next week, some after the harvest, some quietly struck through when the debtor dies.
human_question: Does everything we owe, or are owed, eventually come due?

premise.story: A small rural shopkeeper's credit book, followed through a season of transactions, from money added to accounts to money finally settled or written off.
premise.place: A small grocery shop (kade) in a hill-country tea-growing village.
premise.experience: Worn pages, a shopkeeper's memory for who owes what, customers settling accounts at the counter, and the occasional quiet page where a name is crossed out for good.

concept_links.why: The source's own image for action that never ripens is seed grain kept past its season, which will not sprout [C057-P:L87]. A shop's credit book, where some debts are paid and others simply lapse, gives that idea an entirely secular, everyday form.

what_camera_could_observe: Customers settling or adding to accounts
A conversation about an old account that will never be paid
what_must_be_real: The shop's actual business and its real customers' privacy. Named debts and amounts are never shown identifiably.

possible_arc.opening: The shop opening, the ledger taken down from its shelf.
possible_arc.turn: An old account is mentioned that everyone knows will never be settled.
possible_arc.ending_open: The shop closes for the night. The ledger goes back on its shelf, unfinished as ever.

requirements: A working village shop with a handwritten credit system and a shopkeeper willing to be filmed
Customers willing to be filmed at the counter, or filming arranged to protect their privacy

suggestions.name: A tea-estate village shop in the Nuwara Eliya or Uda Pussellawa area
suggestions.why: Small rural shops with long-running credit books are still common in tea-growing hill country.

risks: Exposing named debtors or a family's money troubles
The metaphor overwhelming the shopkeeper's real livelihood
drop_if: The shopkeeper cannot protect customers' privacy while still telling the story
No shop with the right kind of long-running ledger can be found

connections.note: A second everyday image, a ledger instead of a cattle pen, for the same idea about what comes due and when.
Both ask what happens to what is still owed, or unfinished, when the person involved is gone.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
